reviews.publisherImpact: The HTTP/2 server can refund connection-level flow control twice for the same data: Once when a client resets a stream (refunding data for any sent-but-unread portion of the stream), and again when a request handler reads the buffered data. A malicious client can exploit this to bypass the configured connection-level flow control limit (MaxReceiveBufferPerConnection). Total buffered data is still limited by the concurrent stream limit and stream-level flow control.
reviews.decision: Publisher describes connection-limit bypass with total buffer bounded by stream/concurrency limits. This supports process resource-exhaustion review, but actual server/configuration/system isolation needs proof before routine disposition.
missingProof: For every matched component/location, bind actual ELF/Go metadata OS, file hash, compiler/module version and all aliases on exact candidate.
Review server limits and isolation across container/VPN/development tools; bounded buffers per stream do not by themselves establish host OOM is impossible.
